summary: Ryoshu Kouda specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied under Seitatsu Matsunami. Kouda held researcher posts at Taisho University (attested 1998) and the Hasegawa Institute for Buddhist Culture (attested 2006).

Ryoshu Michihata (1903–1993) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Otani University (~1924–1928). He later held posts at Otani University (~1934–1971) and served as a professor at Kyoto Koka Women's University (~1971–1980).
Ryoshu Misaki (1921–2010) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (~1941–1944). He later served as professor emeritus at Waseda University (~1988–2010).

Ryoshun Okubo (b. 1954) studied Buddhist studies at Waseda University (~1973–1982). He became Professor of Sino-Japanese Buddhism at Waseda University (~2004) and served as director of Taimon Kenkyūkai (attested 2007).
Ryoso Matsushita is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Daishun Ueyama. Matsushita held a lecturer position at Ryukoku University (attested 1987).
Ryota Nakamura works in Buddhist studies, pursuing doctoral studies at Toyo University (attested 2015). In 2015, Nakamura held researcher posts at Toyo University and the Shinran Buddhist Center.

Ryotai Hatai (1883–1974) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held posts at Kyoto University (1929–1943) and served as professor emeritus at Ryukoku University (~1953–1974), teaching Gadjin Nagao and Ryogon Fukuhara.

Ryudo Fujii studied Indology and philosophy under Albrecht Wezler and Harunaga Isaacson. Fujii's academic posts include positions at JSPS (attested 2003), Kokushikan University (attested 2010), and Kyoto Women's University (attested 2015).

Ryugen Taga (b. 1931) studied Buddhist studies at Rissho University (~1953–1955). He spent his career at Rissho University as lecturer (~1958–1966), associate professor (~1966–1974), professor (~1974–2002), and president (~1992–1998).

Ryugen Tanemura (b. 1968) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. Tanemura held posts at Nishogakusha University (attested 2013), Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2014), and Taisho University (attested 2014–2018).

Ryuichi Abe (b. 1954) studied at Keio University, SAIS, and Columbia University. A scholar of Buddhism, Japanology, and religion, he served as professor at Columbia (~1991–2006) and became the Reischauer Institute Professor at Harvard University (~2006).

Ryuichi Kogachi (b. 1970) is a Sinologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1989–2000). He held posts at Kyoto University's Research Centre for the Cultural Sciences (~2001) and Kyoto University as research assistant (~2001–2007) and associate professor (~2007–2018).

Ryujo Yamada (1895–1979) studied at Tokyo Imperial University and under Sylvain Lévi. He held posts at Ryukoku University (~1925–1942), Musashino University (attested 1963), and Tohoku University, where he served as professor (~1942–1958) and professor emeritus (~1958–1979).

Ryuken Sato (1930–2018) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. His career posts included serving as professor emeritus at Taisho University (attested 2014) and advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2014).
Ryusei Keira specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Keira studied at the University of Lausanne, completing a thesis in 2003 under the supervision of Tom J. F. Tillemans.

Ryushin Uryuzu (1932–2015) studied Buddhist studies at Ryukoku University (~1951–1955). He held a post at the Tibetan Tripitaka Research Center (attested 1962) and served as a professor at Kyoto Women's University (~1974–1998).
Ryusho Onami (b. 1926) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taishun Mibu. He served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1985).

Ryuta Kikutani works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Kikutani held posts as a researcher at Tohoku University (attested 2015) and at Kyoto University's Hakubi Center and Graduate School of Letters (attested 2020).

Ryutaro Tsuchida (b. 1947) studied Indology at the University of Tokyo and the University of Marburg, where Wilhelm Rau supervised his doctoral studies. He later served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (~1983–2012).
Ryuzan Nishimoto (1891–1974) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Chishu Kitagawa and Chijo Kitagawa in 1916.
